commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Require virtualenv 21.14.13 or newer in both environments (#10745)

Require virtualenv 21.14.13 or newer in the workspace and standalone
evalchemy environment to address CVE-2026-115586. Refresh both lockfiles
without changing other resolved packages.

The required lint advisory review is incomplete, so this draft is not
ready for merge. Lockfile consistency and diff-scoped lint passed.
Results from broader tests could not be recovered after validation was
interrupted; no security regression test result is claimed.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[marina] Consolidate app sources and retire the applet distinction (#10767)

Consolidate maintained Marina source under `infra/marina/apps/` and use
“app” for both checked-in and ad hoc packages. Check in source when
future changes are expected; ad hoc means no future changes are
expected. If maintenance becomes necessary later, preserve the app's
existing UUID when checking in its source.

Replace `marina applets` with `marina apps`, rename the application
skill to `marina-app`, and update examples, loader flags, imports, agent
source paths, and operational guidance.

All apps release versioned code to Postgres through `marina release`;
named apps add routes and infrastructure-approved capabilities. Preserve
stable UUIDs, the stored `applet.toml`/`applet_id` format, runtime APIs,
and database identifiers so retained revisions remain usable. Moving
source does not release applications or load data.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Keep JAX peers aligned across retries and extend Datakit canary waits (#10759)

Make JAX peers discover the coordinator using task 0's current attempt.
In the October 28 Grug multislice canary, task 0 reached attempt 5 while
task 1 reached attempt 3. Task 1 polled its own attempt name, then timed
out; task 0 exited after the JAX registration deadline. The peer now
refreshes task 0's attempt during discovery, including after a retry.

Extend the Datakit Tier 1 and Tier 2 Actions waits to 20,200 seconds. On
October 28, the Iris jobs succeeded about 4h44m and 5h26m after
submission, after their 7,100- and 14,400-second CI waits expired. The
new wait leaves about 13 minutes under the 350-minute Actions job limit
for diagnostics. Worker placement can still delay either ferry when
cluster memory is scarce.

The [incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/892) holds the
diagnostic steps. PR #10420 also changes JAX endpoint names to isolate
sibling jobs. Preserve both naming rules when merging these branches.

Fixes #10755. Part of #10752.

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[harbor] Strip drop_params from OpenAI requests (#10657)

Remove the LiteLLM-only `drop_params` option before sending Mini-SWE
requests through the OpenAI SDK. Mini-SWE's default YAML sets it, but
`Completions.create` rejects it now that we deprecated LiteLLM, so
trials fail before generation and are scored as model failures. Other
request options pass through unchanged.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Require OAuthLib 4 in affected locked environments (#10749)

Require OAuthLib >=4.0.0 in the root, SkyRL and Harbor environments and
refresh their independent locks. Only OAuthLib changes version.
Evalchemy and Grafana already lock OAuthLib 4 and retain their versions.

This addresses
[GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc),
which affects the previous 3.3.1 locks. The [4.0.0
release](https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/releases/tag/v4.0.0)
removes token-revocation JSONP and validates grant type before client
authentication. Keep the major update separate from [the other
dependency patches](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10748)
for compatibility review. No observed exploitation is claimed.

The three locks pass offline freshness checks. Required diff-scoped lint
and branch advisory review complete with no findings. Harbor's offline
runtime passes 987 tests and all 3 acquisition tests pass. Positive
compatibility probes pass with requests-oauthlib 2.0.0 and
google-auth-oauthlib 1.2.2 from the root lock: a client-credentials
exchange, bearer use, and a Google authorization-code flow with
token-to-credentials conversion. Every HTTP response is mocked with
synthetic credentials. Live identity-provider login and custom
authorization-server integrations remain untested.

Rigging's 21 authentication tests pass. The macOS root suite reports
3,064 passed, 11 skipped and 5 expected failures, with one Linux-only
bubblewrap failure and four collection errors from missing optional
Torch. All five issues reproduce on unchanged main 755a737. Linux CI
passes at bb8248dc17, including Evalchemy, SkyRL, Harbor and the
Levanter Torch/TPU lanes. The affected-test runner's broad command omits
the test group, so the root suite was run with `uv run --frozen
--package marin-core --group test pytest -n 2`, preserving default
safety markers.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Add an allowlist egress policy and make it the CI default (#10538)

Add `EGRESS_POLICY_ALLOWLIST`. An allowlisted task keeps access to the
controller, finelog, other tasks and cluster nodes, but reaches outside
the cluster only through an allowlist. The allowlist combines Iris's
base list (`BASE_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST`: package indexes, Astral's uv
installer, GitHub, Hugging Face, Google Cloud APIs, Weights & Biases and
the Iris dashboards on `*.oa.dev`), the cluster's
`defaults.egress_allowlist.allow`, and the job's own rules. Users add
rules with `iris job run --egress-allow` or
`IrisClient.submit(egress_allow=...)`. A rule is a domain, a one-label
wildcard pattern or a CIDR, optionally limited to TCP ports; a job
carries at most 64, counting those it inherits. Rules take effect when
the job runs under ALLOWLIST and have no effect elsewhere, so a launcher
can declare the hosts its jobs need on every cluster. The controller
stores a job's rules in a new `job_config.egress_allow_json` column
(migration 0053).

When `defaults.egress_allowlist.default` is set, the controller resolves
an unspecified policy to ALLOWLIST for every job except SANDBOX jobs. A
child job inherits its parent's policy and rules, so `--egress-policy
EGRESS_POLICY_CLUSTER` on a root job opts out the whole tree. Only
cw-us-west-04a sets the default here.

Kubernetes enforces the policy with Cilium when
`kubernetes_provider.cilium` is set. Other Kubernetes clusters run
ALLOWLIST jobs under CLUSTER and the controller logs a warning, so
launchers can request the allowlist while clusters gain enforcement.
`iris cluster start` creates a namespace-wide CiliumNetworkPolicy. A job
with its own rules also gets a per-pod policy, applied after the pod is
created and owned by it, so Kubernetes deletes the policy with the pod.
The pod's required Secret volume is written after the policy, so its
containers start only once the policy exists. Cilium's DNS proxy answers
unlisted names with REFUSED, so lookups fail at once. The DNS rules
admit every cluster search-domain candidate up to nine labels, because
musl-based tools such as uv fail a whole lookup at the first refused
candidate. `toFQDNs` does not admit in-cluster addresses, so CoreWeave's
node-local LOTA cache behind `cwlota.com` needs a
`cilium.egress_endpoints` selector. On a host-network cluster, the
controller resolves a GPU job with more than one task to CLUSTER: NCCL
needs the nodes' InfiniBand devices through host networking, which pod
policy cannot restrict. Without `kubernetes_provider.cilium`, pods of
stored ALLOWLIST jobs start on the cluster network, so removing Cilium
from the config rolls the allowlist back. The dashboard's job page shows
the egress policy a job runs under and its rules.

Docker workers accept ALLOWLIST as best effort. The task runs on the
host network, and the worker runs a per-task resolver on a loopback
address in 127.53.0.0/16 that refuses unlisted names. Connections to
literal addresses are not filtered.

The eval launcher declares the hosts its evaluations reach beyond the
base list: Daytona for Harbor evals on Daytona, Harbor's Supabase
registry for registry datasets, an Evalchemy judge's host, and
tiktoken's download host for MRCR. A connection survey of the three
production CoreWeave clusters found 23 of 346 running task pods, each
from a different root job, reaching hosts outside the base list; 11 of
those jobs were Harbor evals.

Default job environments turn off vendor telemetry with
`DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1`, `RAY_USAGE_STATS_ENABLED=0`
and `WANDB_ERROR_REPORTING=false`. vLLM and Ray usage stats, Hugging
Face Hub telemetry and W&B's own crash reports would otherwise be
refused under the allowlist. W&B run logging is unchanged.

The allowlist limits accidental and casual exfiltration. Allowlisted
services such as GitHub and Cloud Storage can still carry data out.

A cluster that sets `kubernetes_provider.cilium` needs the controller
ClusterRole's Cilium policy rule from #10548, granting create and patch,
applied with `pulumi up` before it deploys this controller. Until then,
`iris cluster start` reports the missing rule and stops before changing
the deployment.
